full_judgment:
Feeling aggrieved by a Judgment recorded by appellate Court allowing a Preemption Miscellaneous Case laid under section 96 of The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (for short The Act) reversing Judgment passed by trial Court dismissing Preemption Miscellaneous Case, one of the pre-emptees as petitioner approached this Court in a Revision Petition under section 115 of The Code of Civil Procedure (shortly The Code). 

 3. The precise facts forming background of this Revision Petition are stated succinctly hereunder.

 The word is further defined as meaning release or abandonment of one's rights, if, having rights, he stands by and sees another dealing with his property in a manner inconsistent with such rights, and makes no objection while the act is in progress; resting apparently satisfied, without objection; resting satisfied with or submission to an existing state of things; silence and inaction; silent but conscious consent; silent passive assent; submission; tacit encouragement. 

 "Acquiescence" as stated in Wharton's Law Lexicon Fourteenth. Edition is consent, either express or implied. 

 26. OPW 1 who is no other than Pre-emptee- Petitioner in his evidence (examination-in-chief) stated that on 2-9-1994 (Friday) after Jumma Prayer Hashim Majumdar, Ismail Prodhania and Junab Ali had been present and Chairman Jethajee (Pre- emptor No. 4 Md Zonab Ali Talukder) and Ali Newaz Master settled consideration money. In cross-examination he stated that during talk Pre-emptor No.4 (Chairman) and Pre-emptor No.6. Zainal Abedin, Abdul Matin Talukder, Abul Kalam Talukder, Momin Ullah Talukder, Abdul Matin Sarker, Ismail Prodhania, Junab Ali, Hashim, Momataz, his father and he himself had been present. He further stated that consideration money had been settled by Pre-emptor No. 4 and Pre-emptor No. 6 Doctor Zainal Abedin. Ismail Prodhania, the person allegedly present at the time of sitting (Mojlish) as OPW No. 2 stated that Chairman Md. Zonab Ali Talukder (Pre-emptor No. 4), Ali Newaz Master, Abul Kalam, father of Pre- emptee-Petitioner, Junab Ali and he himself had been present and Pre-emptor No. 4 settled the consideration money of the sale. On a careful scrutiny and examination of the testimonies of OPW 1 who is Pre-emptor-Petitioner and OPW 2 Ismail Prodhania, it appears that their testimonies suffer from inconsistencies and, also, contradictions. In order to deprive a co-sharer in getting a Statutory right of Pre-emption on the question of Waiver and Acquiescence there must be strict proof with consistent testimonies by reliable witnesses. It reveals that persons who were alleged to have been present at the alleged sitting had not been examined in support of contention raised by Pre-emptee- Petitioner, Inconsistencies occurred in testimonies of OPWs 1 and 2 had been, also, noticed, discussed and considered by learned Appellate Judge. Moreover, no case had been made out nor any legal evidence had been produced by Pre-emptees that Pre-emptors voluntarily surrendered or relinquished the known legal right and neglected to exercise right of Pre-emption after the Transfer by which the right of Pre-emption stood barred by law. 

 30. Decisions of Court of Appeal being last and final court of fact are not open to interference in Revisional Jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code unless it is shown that decisions have been based upon gross misreading of evidence or those have been founded on misconception or misapplication or misapprehension of law or of any misinterpretation of any material document or otherwise perverse being contrary to law, evidence and materials brought on record. Support for the above proposition is sought to be drawn from a series of decisions, both of our Jurisdiction and foreign Jurisdictions. Mussammat Durga Choudhurain vs Jawahir Singh Choudhuri, 17 Indian Appeal 122, Ramchandra vs Ram Lingam, AIR 1963 SC 302, Abdul Mazid and others vs Khalil Ahmed, PLD 1955 FC 38, Azizur Rahman vs Per Vaizshan and others 1997 PSC 1329, Fazal Karim vs Abdul Manafard and others 1997 PSC 1163, Federal Radid Commission vs Nelson Brothers Board and Mortgage Company and others (1932) 289 US 266, Virgina Electric and Power Company vs National Relations Board (1942) 319 US 533, Guejt Heluering, Commissioner of International Revenue vs John Kehoe, (1939) 309 US 267, State of New York and others vs United States of America (1946) 331 US 284, Fakhruddin Mia and another vs Mohammad Khoda Baksh Sheikh, 29 DLR (SC) 268, Akrab Ali vs ZahiruddinKari 30 DLR SC 81, Abdul Matin Chowdhuryvs Chapala Rani Sen and others, 37 DLR (AD) 205, Naimuddin Sardar vs Md Abdul Kalam Biswas 41DLR (AD) 3, Jasimuddin Kanchan vs Md Ali Ashraf 42 DLR (AD) 289, Mazhurul Borhan vs AH Bhuiyan 1995 BLD (AD) 237 and Haider Unnessa and another vs Monowara Begum and others 1996 BLD (AD) 280 are some authorities for the aforesaid proposition.
